parts.text: A student investigates the image produced by a lens. Fig. 3.1 shows the apparatus. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • The student places the lens a distance u = 20.0 cm from the illuminated object. • He moves the screen until a clearly focused image is formed on the screen. • He measures the distance v between the centre of the lens and the screen. • Calculate, and record in the first row of Table 3.1, u v . • He repeats the procedure for u = 25.0 cm, u = 30.0 cm, u = 35.0 cm and u = 40.0 cm. The readings and results are shown in Table 3.1. Table 3.1 u / cm v / cm u v 20.0 79.5 25.0 44.5 0.56 30.0 35.0 0.86 35.0 30.0 1.17 40.0 27.0 1.48 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of u / cm ( y -axis) against u v ( x -axis). Start the y -axis at u = 15.0 cm. [4]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text:
axes correctly labelled with quantity and unit and right way round
suitable scales with u axis starting at 15.0
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Use your graph to find u 1 , the value of u when u v = 1.0. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. u 1 = .................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
method clearly shown on graph
value correct to within ½ small square

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate the focal length f of the lens using the equation f = u 1 2 . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. f = .............................................. cm [2]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
Correct value for f – candidate’s (c) ÷ 2
to 2 or 3 significant figures

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
Read both parts of the answer together and award the marks in either order
deciding the screen position for most clearly focused image
move screen slowly / backwards and forwards
OR
the image is difficult to see
carry out in a darkened room / away from bright lights
OR
(metre) rule moving
clamp rule / tape rule to bench
OR
the image is (small and) difficult to focus
use a bigger object
OR
difficult to find the centre of the lens
use a marked lens holder
OR
object, (centre of) lens (and screen) are not at the same height above the bench
use a ruler / set-square to check
